title: Enterprise Prospect Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview

Summary
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, an executive pitch-deck outline, practical pricing guidance, two enterprise case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this doc for AE/SE enablement when selling Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity), or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem).

Target audience
- Account Executives (AEs) and Sales Engineers (SEs)
- Solution and Pre-Sales Engineers
- Customer Success managers for onboarding conversations

Use cases covered
- Rapid proof-of-value (hosted API)
- Predictable production throughput (Dedicated)
- Regulated or air-gapped deployments (Private)

Elevator pitch (30s)
Redwood Inference provides a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, high-performance LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We optimize for throughput, latency, reliability, and cost so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building or operating a custom inference stack.

Key positioning pillars (for messaging)
1) Production-first economics
- Emphasize unit-cost controls: batching, KV-caching, quantization profiles, and routing policies.
- Talk ROI: reduce per-token cost by 2-5x vs unmanaged self-hosted setups for similar latency targets.
2) Unified runtime and consistent API
- Single API surface across Hosted API, Dedicated, Private. Same SDKs, same rollout controls, same tracing and metrics in Redwood Console.
3) Reliability and graceful degradation
- Smart routing and model fallbacks keep applications online: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> cross-region fallback.
4) Enterprise readiness
- Private deployment, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and compliance evidence packages (SOC2/ISO27001).

Persona messaging (short snippets)
- Engineering/Platform: "Ship faster with a GPU-optimized runtime (continuous batching, KV cache management, optimized kernels) and predictable throughput. Focus on product, not ops."
- Product/PM: "Consistent API and rollout controls let you run A/B model rollouts and quickly iterate on prompt sets without unpredictable infra costs."
- Security/Legal: "Private deployment with customer-managed VPC, KMS integration, and auditable logs. We provide compliance evidence and contractual protections for data residency and retention."

Competitive brief (one-pager)
Top competitors: Managed cloud AI endpoints (cloud-A, cloud-B), LLM API providers (api-X, api-Y), inference infra vendors (infraCo).
Differentiators (how to position vs each):
- vs cloud-A / cloud-B: Redwood provides a single developer experience plus optimized inference runtime for lower unit cost and predictable latency at scale. Emphasize model routing and fallback policies which cloud endpoints lack.
- vs api-X / api-Y: Our advantage is dedicated capacity and private deployment options with enterprise controls; not just a hosted black box.
- vs infraCo (self-hosted runtimes): Redwood saves operational effort and provides strong observability and rollout tooling; avoids lock-in to a single hardware configuration.

Quick competitive matrix (simplified)
Capability | Redwood | cloud-A | api-X | infraCo (self-host)
---|---:|:---:|:---:|:---:  
Unified API (hosted/dedicated/private) | Yes | Partial | No | No
Production SLOs & SLA | SLA (Dedicated) | SLA | No | Depends
Enterprise Private / VPC | Yes | Partial | No | Yes
Cost controls (batch/caching/quantization) | Advanced | Limited | Limited | Advanced
Observability & Rollouts | Built-in Redwood Console | Basic | Limited | Tooling required

Pitch deck outline and speaker notes
Slide 1 — Title / Hook (30s)
- Problem: Teams building LLM features face unpredictable latency, ballooning costs, and ops overhead.
- Hook line: "Treat model serving as a platform problem — make inference predictable."

Slide 2 — Product at a glance (45s)
- Redwood API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private + Redwood Console + Redwood Optimize.
- One-liner and 3 bullets: predictable latency, lower unit cost, enterprise controls.

Slide 3 — How it works (60s)
- Serving runtime: continuous batching, KV cache, quantization-friendly paths.
- Smart routing: policy-driven routing with fallbacks.
- Diagram: request -> router -> runtime pool (primary/quantized/fallback) -> Redwood Console metrics (describe diagram in bullets).

Slide 4 — Value / ROI (60s)
- Example: customer with 2M monthly tokens saves estimated 45% in monthly inference costs after switching to Dedicated + batching optimizations.
- Show baseline vs Redwood with a short table of latency and cost.

Slide 5 — Security & Compliance (45s)
- Private deployment options, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC2/ISO readiness.

Slide 6 — Case studies (90s)
- Two short stories (see Case Studies section below) with metrics and quote.

Slide 7 — Pricing & engagement model (60s)
- High-level tiers and what to propose for typical prospect profiles (see Pricing Guidance).

Slide 8 — Next steps / trial offers (30s)
- Hosted proof-of-value (API keys + event-level tracing) or Dedicated POC (time-boxed capacity reservation).

Pricing guidance (field playbook)
Principles
- Start with customer intent: prototype -> production -> regulated production. Align product recommendation to this lifecycle.
- Be explicit about cost drivers: tokens, concurrency, throughput (tokens/s), and model family.
- Use Redwood Optimize to generate batching/quantization recommendations before quoting.

Recommended offers
1) Hosted API (self-serve) — best for quick proofs of value
- Pricing: usage-based per-token for generate/chat and per-embedding unit for embeddings. Typical list price bands: $0.0008–$0.005 / 1k tokens depending on model size and latency.
- When to propose: <500k monthly tokens or early-stage proof.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — best for predictable production at scale
- Pricing model: monthly committed capacity + overage; tiers based on GPU pool size and target throughput.
- Example guidance: small Dedicated pool (8 A100-equivalent GPUs) starts at ~$30k/month list for enterprise packages; medium (32 GPUs) and large (64+) scale with discounting. Always consult pricing desk for exact quotes.
- Discounting rules: typical annual commit discounts 10–25% depending on term and commitment.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — best for regulated or data-residency sensitive customers
- Pricing model: platform licensing + deployment/ops professional services; pricing varies by infra and SRE support level.
- When to propose: required by compliance, data residency, or air-gapped needs.

How to present ROI to a prospect (one-page)
1) Capture baseline: current monthly tokens, average generation length, concurrency, and latency targets.
2) Estimate Redwood config: model variant, batching and cache assumptions, and Dedicated sizing.
3) Produce comparison: monthly cost, expected P95 latency, and operational burden (FTEs saved).
4) Example: 10M tokens/month baseline cost $60k (self-host + ops) vs Redwood Dedicated estimated $32k/month (including ops), net run-rate savings $28k/mo.

Discounting & contracting playbook
- For deals > $250k ARR: escalate to SalesOps and Legal for playbook discounts and custom SLAs.
- For Private deployments: require 60–90 day provisioning lead time in contract. Document expected delivery milestones (installation, testing, cutover).

Case studies (concise)
1) FinTech: Ledgerly (anonymized) — use case: real-time document summarization and KYC form parsing
- Deployment: Dedicated (32-GPU pool) + Private control plane for regional data residency.
- Outcome in first 90 days: 3x throughput improvement vs previous self-hosted stack; 38% reduction in per-token cost via batching & KV caching; P95 latency dropped from 560ms to 180ms.
- Quote: "Redwood shortened our path to production and gave us confidence at scale." — VP Engineering (Ledgerly).

2) Consumer SaaS: ComposeAI (anonymized) — use case: in-product code completions and contextual search
- Deployment: Hosted API -> Dedicated for production traffic.
- Outcome: 2x model iteration velocity due to rollout tools; 47% cost savings after switching to quantized variant for low-priority traffic.

Security FAQ (prospect-facing)
Q1: How does Redwood handle customer data sent to the Hosted API?
A1: For Hosted API, request payloads and generated outputs are processed transiently by Redwood. By default, Redwood does not use customer data to train models. Logs and payloads are retained for a default of 30 days for debugging and abuse monitoring; retention can be reduced or disabled under contract. For sensitive workloads, recommend Redwood Private.

Q2: Do you support Bring Your Own Key (BYOK)?
A2: Yes. For Dedicated and Private, we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed keys for encryption of at-rest snapshots and secret material.

Q3: What compliance evidence is available?
A3: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II report, ISO27001 certificate, and PCI-DSS guidance where applicable. For enterprise customers we provide compliance evidence packages and can support third-party audits under NDA.

Q4: How are logs and audit trails handled for Private deployments?
A4: Private deployments ship audit logs to customer-managed logging endpoints (S3, CloudWatch, Stackdriver) or to a secured Redwood-managed storage depending on contract. All API calls and admin actions are logged with user ID, timestamp, and request metadata.

Q5: What are your SLOs and SLAs?
A5: Hosted API: best-effort with published performance profiles per model. Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime (typically 99.9% monthly uptime for enterprise contracts). Latency targets are defined per-reservation tier (e.g., P50 60–120ms for token generation for small models; P95 targets vary with sequence length and model family). Include SLA language during procurement.

Q6: Data residency and retention controls?
A6: For Dedicated and Private we support region pinning and customer-controlled retention policies. Example contractual terms: data residency guarantee (region-level) and deletion confirmation within 30 days of termination for Hosted records; Private deployments subject to customer retention controls.

Q7: Vulnerability management and incident response?
A7: Redwood maintains a vulnerability and patching cadence for the runtime and control plane. We offer an incident response process (RFC/IR playbook), provide incident summaries for security-impacting events, and escalate to customer SOCs for serious incidents. See related page: /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security.

Demo & PoC checklist (SE-run)
1) Discovery call: capture volumes (tokens/mo), latency targets, model families, compliance constraints.
2) Hosted quickstart: provision API key, sample prompt set, enable event-level tracing in Redwood Console.
3) Dedicated PoC: provision time-boxed Dedicated pool (8–32 GPUs), run benchmarking harness (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite), collect P50/P95/P99 latency and throughput curves.
4) Private POC: share deployment requirements (VPC/subnet ranges, KMS details), schedule on-prem packaging window, validate audit log pipeline.

SE checklist commands (examples)
- Provisioning (Hosted):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/keys -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"name":"poc-key"}'

- Small benchmark sample (pseudo):
  python tools/benchmark.py --api-key $POC_KEY --model rdw-instruct-70b-8k-quant --concurrency 16 --duration 300
